'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**Six people are killed and three others are kidnapped as [[Islamist]]s [[insurgent]]s raid the districts of [[Eráti District|Erati]] and [[Memba District|Memba]], [[Mozambique]], torching dozens of houses. Six attackers are arrested.
**Gunmen storm the [[Comboni Missionary Sisters]]' church in Chipene, Mozambique, killing an [[Italians|Italian]] nun and setting ablaze the church, the nuns' homes and the hospital. Two other nuns and two priests escaped. [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2022/09/07/italian-nun-killed-in-terror-attack-in-mozambique_0e99ac8a-3cc4-4120-9f96-299053ad0245.html (Ansa)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Fights erupt in the village of [[Talataye]] between the [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara|Islamic State]], [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] and the [[National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad]], with the [[Malian Armed Forces]] launching [[airstrike]]s amid the fighting. At least 30 people are killed. [https://crisis24.garda.com/alerts/2022/09/mali-further-armed-clashes-likely-following-sept-6-militant-attack-on-talataye-in-gao-region (Crisis24)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Twenty [[Southern Transitional Council]] [[Separatism|separatist]] fighters are killed by [[Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula|al-Qaeda]] gunmen in [[Abyan Governorate]]. All of the six attackers are also killed in the [[gunfight]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/9/6/al-qaeda-attack-kills-yemeni-forces-in-abyan-southern-army-says (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Anglophone Crisis]]
**Six people are killed and eight others are injured when separatists [[mass shootings|open fire]] on a public bus in [[Southwest Region (Cameroon)|South West]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-six-civilians-killed-after-cameroon-separatists-open-fire-bus-2022-09-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Pacific typhoon season]]
**Ten people are killed in [[South Korea]] by [[Typhoon Hinnamnor]]. Seven of the victims died in a flooded underground car park. In addition, 2,900 people are [[emergency evacuation|evacuated]] and 66,000 homes are damaged. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62816374 (BBC News)]
*[[September 2022 Afghanistan earthquake]]
**Six people are killed when two [[earthquake]]s strike northern [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/two-earthquakes-rattle-afghanistan-killing-least-six-2022-09-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Binh Duong karaoke bar fire]]
**At least 32 people are killed in a karaoke bar fire in [[Bình Dương province|Binh Duong]], [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-62816377 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Africa floods]]
**[[2022 Chad floods]]
***Thousands of people evacuate in [[N'Djamena]], [[Chad]], due to extensive flooding caused by the country's heaviest rains in 30 years. An estimated 442,000 [[Chadians]] have been impacted by the floods since the end of August. [https://www.msn.com/en-xl/weather/other/thousands-battle-catastrophic-floods-after-chad-s-heaviest-rains-in-30-years/ar-AA11vqmL (Reuters)]
*A [[car crash]] in south [[Sydney]], [[Australia]] kills 5 children and leaves an 18-year-old driver with minor injuries. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/driver-refused-bail-to-face-court-following-deaths-of-five-teenagers-killed-in-sydney-crash/91oj3o08v (SBS)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]] approves a nasal [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to combat [[COVID-19]], becoming the second country to do so after [[China]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/india-approves-its-first-nasal-vaccine-covid-19-2923076 (CNA)]
*[[2022 monkeypox outbreak]]
**[[2022 monkeypox outbreak in Asia]]
***[[Hong Kong]] confirms its first case of [[monkeypox]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/hong-kong-discovers-first-case-monkeypox-2022-09-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[2022 monkeypox outbreak in the United States]]
***[[Wisconsin]] and [[North Carolina]] expand their eligibility for the [[smallpox vaccine|monkeypox vaccine]] in at-risk communities. [https://wpde.com/amp/news/local/north-carolina-monkeypox-vacine-eligibility-high-risk-category-cdc (WPDE-TV)] [https://www.jsonline.com/story/news/health/2022/09/06/wisconsin-monkeypox-vaccine-eligibility-criteria-expands-black-community-most-impacted/8000987001/ (''Milwaukee Journal Sentinel'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2022 Kiribati constitutional crisis]]
**[[Kiribati]] suspends three retired [[New Zealand]] judges from the [[Kiribati Court of Appeal]] as the [[constitutional crisis]] worsens. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/kiribati-suspends-appeals-court-judges-constitutional-crisis-worsens-2022-09-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[January 6 United States Capitol attack]]
**[[Couy Griffin]], a [[commissioner]] of [[Otero County, New Mexico]], [[United States]], is barred from public office by a state judge due to his involvement in the January 6 attack, which was determined to be an [[insurrection]]. This is the first time that the [[Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fourteenth Amendment]] has been used in more than a century to ban a person who participated in an insurrection from serving in the government. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/06/us/politics/jan-6-griffin-insurrection.html (''New York Times'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/09/06/politics/couy-griffin-new-mexico-january-6/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[July 2022 Conservative Party leadership election|2022 Conservative Party leadership election]]
**[[Liz Truss]] succeeds [[Boris Johnson]] to become [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/liz-truss-becomes-prime-minister-of-the-uk-12691158 (Sky News)]
*One person is killed during [[Anti-MONUSCO protests|anti-U.N. protests]] in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-one-dead-latest-anti-un-protest-east-congo-2022-09-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts'''
*[[Stable Diffusion|An AI Artist is open sourced]]
**[[Artificial intelligence art]] meets [[Open Source]]. A model that cost $600000 [https://the-decoder.com/training-cost-for-stable-diffusion-was-just-600000-and-that-is-a-good-sign-for-ai-progress/ (The Decoder)] to train, is released for use by anyone, stirring controversy about creativity and the future of art, artists and digital illustrators.
